original_question: For a graph G, let chi_l(G) be the least integer k such that every k-list-assignment L admits a proper L-coloring, and let chi*_l(G) be the least integer k such that for every k-list-assignment L, the graph G admits an L-packing of size k, meaning k pairwise-disjoint L-colorings. Does there exist a graph G for which the list packing number exceeds the list-chromatic number by at least 2, that is, chi*_l(G) > chi_l(G) + 1?
target_in_paper: Section 2, "Various open problems related to list packing," under "The list packing conjecture," Problem 2.1: "Is there a graph G for which χ^*_ℓ(G) > χ_ℓ(G) + 1?" ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's intended problem almost verbatim: it concerns arbitrary graphs G, uses the correct parameters χ_ℓ(G) and χ^*_ℓ(G), defines χ^*_ℓ(G) via k pairwise-disjoint proper L-colourings for every k-list-assignment L, and asks exactly whether the gap can be at least 2, i.e. whether χ^*_ℓ(G) > χ_ℓ(G)+1. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))
missing_details: The paper makes explicit that a k-list-assignment is a function L:V(G)→2^N such that each list L(v) has size k, i.e. each vertex receives a k-element subset of the natural numbers. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))

An L-colouring is explicitly a map c:V(G)→N with c(v)∈L(v) for every vertex v; it is proper when c(u)≠c(v) for every edge uv. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))

Two L-colourings c_i and c_j are disjoint in the pointwise sense: c_i(u)≠c_j(u) for every vertex u∈V(G). ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))

For χ^*_ℓ(G), the quantifier is: for every k-list-assignment L of G, there must exist k pairwise-disjoint proper L-colourings of G. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))

The problem is posed for an arbitrary graph G, with no added hypotheses such as planarity, bounded degree, bipartiteness, or triangle-freeness. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))

No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or asymptotic "for all sufficiently large" condition is part of this statement; the surrounding discussion introduces only graph/list-colouring notation. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))
refined_question: Let G be a graph. For a positive integer k, a k-list-assignment of G is a function L:V(G)→2^N such that |L(v)|=k for every v∈V(G). An L-colouring of G is a map c:V(G)→N with c(v)∈L(v) for all v∈V(G), and it is proper if c(u)≠c(v) whenever uv∈E(G). Two L-colourings c_i and c_j are disjoint if c_i(v)≠c_j(v) for every v∈V(G). Define χ_ℓ(G) to be the least integer k such that every k-list-assignment L of G admits a proper L-colouring, and define χ^*_ℓ(G) to be the least integer k such that every k-list-assignment L of G admits k pairwise-disjoint proper L-colourings. Is there a graph G such that χ^*_ℓ(G) > χ_ℓ(G)+1? ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))
justification: The draft is aiming at exactly Problem 2.1, not a broader neighboring conjecture. The immediately preceding definitions in Section 2 supply all of the notation needed to make the question fully stand-alone: k-list-assignments, L-colourings, properness, pointwise disjointness, χ_ℓ(G), and χ^*_ℓ(G). The refined version therefore keeps the paper's scope unchanged and only spells out those implicit definitions. The nearby discussion does not give an alternate equivalent formulation of Problem 2.1. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))
